# @triton/sandbox (TypeScript)

TypeScript SDK for Triton sandboxes: Linux microVMs for agents and code.
The surface follows E2B, so moving over is mostly a change of import.

Node 18 or later, and Bun. ESM and CommonJS. Dependency: `ws`.

Not on npm yet. Make a tarball from a checkout, then install it in your
project:

```
cd sdks/typescript && npm ci && npm pack        # writes triton-sandbox-0.1.0.tgz
cd /path/to/your/project && npm install /path/to/triton-sandbox-0.1.0.tgz
```

`npm pack` builds `dist/` first. Keep the tarball next to your project and
commit it, or put it on an internal file server, so a fresh `npm install`
finds it.

## Quickstart, next to E2B

E2B:

```ts
import { Sandbox } from '@e2b/code-interpreter'   // E2B_API_KEY

const sbx = await Sandbox.create({ timeoutMs: 300_000 })
const r = await sbx.commands.run('echo hello')
console.log(r.stdout)
await sbx.files.write('/tmp/a.txt', 'data')
console.log(await sbx.files.read('/tmp/a.txt'))
console.log((await sbx.runCode('1 + 1')).text)
console.log(sbx.getHost(3000))
await sbx.kill()
```

Triton:

```ts
import { Sandbox } from '@triton/sandbox'         // TRITON_URL + TRITON_API_KEY

const sbx = await Sandbox.create({ template: 'code-interpreter', timeoutMs: 300_000 })
const r = await sbx.commands.run('echo hello')
console.log(r.stdout)
await sbx.files.write('/tmp/a.txt', 'data')
console.log(await sbx.files.read('/tmp/a.txt'))
console.log((await sbx.runCode('1 + 1')).text)
const fwd = await sbx.ports.forward(3000)         // previews are coming; see Surface
console.log(fwd.localPort)
await fwd.close()
await sbx.kill()
```

## Work on a GitHub repo

```ts
const githubToken = process.env.GH_TOKEN
const sbx = await Sandbox.create({ repo: 'acme/widget', branch: 'main', githubToken })
await sbx.git(['checkout', '-b', 'fix'])                     // runs in /work/widget
await sbx.commands.run('make test', { cwd: '/work/widget' })
await sbx.git(['commit', '-am', 'Fix the bug'])
await sbx.git(['push', '-u', 'origin', 'fix'], { githubToken })
```

Only github.com repos. The token goes only in the env of the git exec
(clone, fetch, push, ls-remote; run fetch then merge for a pull). It is not stored,
not written to the guest, and is scrubbed from errors. It is refused over
plain http, except to a loopback address, and the request that carries it
does not follow redirects. Egress to GitHub is added to the network policy.

## Credentials

Highest first: options (`apiUrl`, `apiKey`, `accessToken`, `username` and
`password`, `project`), then `TRITON_URL`, `TRITON_API_KEY`,
`TRITON_ACCESS_TOKEN`, `TRITON_USERNAME` and `TRITON_PASSWORD`,
`TRITON_PROJECT`, then the `tritonctl` session (read only). A private CA goes
in `TRITON_DC_ANCHORS` (added to the default roots, as tritonctl does);
`caCert` or `TRITON_CA_CERT` names the only roots to trust.

## Surface

Same as the Python SDK, in camelCase: `Sandbox.create/connect/list/kill`
(`Sandbox.create({ package: 'sandbox-4g' })` picks the size; `sbx.resize('sandbox-8g')` moves a stopped sandbox),
`sbx.commands.run(cmd, { background, onStdout, onStderr, envs, cwd, user, timeoutMs, stdin })`,
`sbx.pty.create/sendStdin/resize`, `sbx.files.read/write/list/getInfo/exists/remove/rename/makeDir/watchDir`,
`sbx.ports.forward/tunnel`, `sbx.getHost(port)`, `sbx.ports.open/list/close`,
`sbx.stop/start/pause/resume/snapshot/fork/resize/setTimeout`, `sbx.runCode(code, { language, context })`,
`sbx.metrics()`, and `sbx.desktop.screenshot/leftClick/doubleClick/write/press/scroll/moveMouse/rdpTunnel`.

Errors are typed: `NotImplementedError` (with `.reason`), `NotFoundError`,
`RateLimitError` (with `.retryAfter`), `SandboxNotRunningError`,
`PersistModeUnsupportedError`, `CommandExitError`, all under `SandboxError`.
`getHost`, `getUrl` and `ports.open` throw `PreviewsDisabledError` (a
`FeatureDisabledError`) until the cloud has a preview domain; reach the
port with `ports.forward` instead.

## Tests

```
npm test     # Node 22.6 or later runs the .ts tests directly
```

The tests start `sdks/testing/mock_triton` (needs `python3`), which checks
every request and answer against the OpenAPI document. No network is used.
